t: Nineveh grew from a farming village of the 6th millennium BCE into a proto-city, a trade colony of Uruk and a provincial town of Assyria before Sennacherib made it a truly influential city around 700 BCE.

It was the capital and largest city of the Neo-Assyrian Empire until a coalition of former subject peoples besieged and sacked it in 612 BCE, after which it was never again a political or administrative centre.

A settlement survived under the Persians, Seleucids, Parthians and Sasanians and became a bishopric of the Church of the East, but it was eclipsed by Mosul and mostly abandoned by the 14th century CE.
dyk: Sennacherib's South West Palace had at least 80 rooms, and the foundation under it was made of roughly 2,680,000 cubic metres of brick, about 160 million bricks.
ev: Nineveh is founded as a farming village in the late Neolithic period
Ashur-uballit I reclaims the city from Mitanni and founds the Middle Assyrian Empire
Sennacherib lays out new streets and squares and builds the South West Palace
A coalition of Babylonians, Medes and Scythians sacks and razes the city
Nineveh is a bishopric of the Church of the East
The Arabs conquer the area and build a mosque on the west bank
Benjamin of Tudela visits the site
Nineveh is mostly abandoned after Timur's massacres and dispersal of Assyrian Christians

f.founded: As early as 6000 BCE, during the late Neolithic period, as a farming village; in the Hebrew Bible (Genesis 10:11) the city is built by Ashur, though some modern translations make Nimrod its founder.
f.where: On the eastern bank of the Tigris at its junction with the Khosr River, on a level part of the plain of Upper Mesopotamia, in the present-day city of Mosul in northern Iraq.
f.known: Capital and largest city of the Neo-Assyrian Empire; Sennacherib's South West Palace; the library of Ashurbanipal; the sack of 612 BCE; the prophet Jonah in the Hebrew Bible and the Quran; the Assyrian sculptures in museums around the world
f.today: The ruins lie across the river from the historical centre of Mosul, and the name Nineveh is also used for the half of Mosul on the eastern bank and for the Nineveh Governorate.
